title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed sheet from a Bourbaki draft (rédaction n° 392, page 6-44), from the exercises of a commutative-algebra chapter on conductor, complementary module (C*) and different. It appears to have been reused in the folder, since the neighbouring handwritten pages concern the functional equation of L-functions. Content, in modern terms:

(End of ex. 5) B is the ring of integers of a number field and C ranges over orders. The visible part is the converse. Take C = Z + pB. Its conductor is f = pB, and C/f ≅ F_p. As a C-module, C/f ≅ C*/B* ≅ B/C, where * denotes the trace dual (complementary module). Comparing orders, p = |B/C| = p^{n-1}, so n = 2. The ex. 5 statement itself is on the previous Bourbaki page and is not visible. The visible fragment only shows that the principality condition just stated forces n = 2, i.e. the field is quadratic. Plausibly the condition is the Gorenstein-type property that C* is principal/invertible, as in Bass's 1963 'ubiquity' theme; this is an inference, not read on the page.

(Ex. 6) Setting: A is a normal noetherian domain, L/K is finite separable, B is the integral closure of A in L, and C is an intermediate finite order (A ⊂ C ⊂ B). Let p be a height-one prime of A and P a prime of C over p. The following are equivalent:
- (a) P does not contain the different D_{C/A} after localizing at p.
- (b) P_p is a primary component of pC_p (multiplicity one) and the residue extension is separable.
- (c) Exactly one prime P' of B lies over P, P' is unramified over p, and the residue fields of P and P' coincide. Equivalently, C is regular/étale at P.
This is the Dedekind different criterion for ramification, extended to non-maximal orders. The hint reduces to A a DVR and uses length computations and semi-local completions.

(Ex. 7) Monogenicity.
- (a) A power basis 1, x, …, x^{n-1} is stable under small perturbation of x.
- (b) Over a DVR, if P has separable residue extension, there is a primitive element x with conductor f_{B/A[x]} prime to P. This is a local primitive-element / index-form statement.
- (c) If p splits completely into n = [L:K] primes, then B = A[x] for some x iff n ≤ |k̄|, where k̄ is the residue field of A. The reason is that B/pB ≅ k̄^n is generated by one element iff n distinct residues exist; Hensel's lemma and the approximation theorem then lift. This is the classical common-index-divisor phenomenon (Dedekind, Hensel).
errors: 'fermeture algébrique de A dans L' should read 'fermeture intégrale'. This is a terminological slip in the typescript.
The proposition number in 7a) and the n° in 7c) are left blank in the draft.
In ex. 6 'composante P-primaire de Cp' means of pC. This is notation, not an error.
The statements appear correct as given. In 7c) the condition n ≤ Card(k̄) is right because each prime has residue degree 1.
